anchor.quote: a recursion's cost per bit can grow as a fixed power of its parameter, with exponent $\lambda<1$
Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$

anchor.note: Big-O notation, covered by the reader profile

anchor.quote: Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: sigma is only given a range; the page never says what it denotes (an auxiliary exponent), and earlier pages bind sigma to unrelated things.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk
gaps.note: The reader is never told what a kernel is or why a leaf costs O(f/m^nu).

gaps.term: row addition cost from interchange cost
gaps.quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
gaps.note: Only the cost of an address interchange is cited; the page never says how a row addition reduces to it or why it costs O(V(u^tau+1)), nor what the fixed number of row additions is.

gaps.quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
gaps.note: Earlier u is a number of bits (u=f*Omega); here u is a number of chunks, with no notice of the change, so the reader cannot check the leaf-cost bound O((s/W)^nu u).
The page also needs lambda<1 and lambda>log_m(s/W), but never states that tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1, so the reader cannot check that a suitable lambda exists.
